title: Reset a lost or broken MFA token for branch staff
author: kb.author.identity
body:
## Symptoms
Branch staff cannot sign in because the authenticator app was removed, the phone was replaced, or the hardware token shows no code.

## Cause
The MFA registration is bound to the old device and must be reset before a new device can be enrolled.

## Resolution
1. Verify the caller's identity with the branch manager call-back procedure; never accept identity details sent by email.
2. In the identity console, open the user and select Reset MFA registration.
3. Ask the user to sign in from a branch workstation and enrol the new device using the on-screen QR code.
4. Confirm a successful test sign-in before closing the request.
5. If the user is travelling and cannot reach a branch workstation, issue a temporary access pass valid for 8 hours and record the approval in the ticket.

title: VPN connection fails with error 809
author: kb.author.network
body:
## Symptoms
The remote access VPN client stops at Connecting and then reports error 809, usually on home or hotel networks.

## Cause
The local router blocks or does not forward the IPsec NAT-T traffic (UDP 4500) that the VPN tunnel needs.

## Resolution
1. Ask the user to switch the VPN profile from IPsec to the SSL profile named CB-Remote-SSL, which uses TCP 443.
2. If the SSL profile also fails, have the user restart the home router and try again on a wired connection.
3. Collect the client log from the Help menu and attach it to the incident.
4. Escalate to CB-Network-Ops only if several users report the same error from different locations, because that points to a gateway problem.

title: VPN error 809 on home networks
author: kb.author.servicedesk
body:
## Symptoms
VPN client shows error 809 when connecting from a home network.

## Cause
The home router blocks IPsec NAT-T traffic on UDP 4500.

## Resolution
1. Switch the VPN profile to CB-Remote-SSL which uses TCP 443.
2. Restart the home router and retry.
3. Attach the VPN client log to the incident.

title: Card authorization timeouts - first response runbook
author: kb.author.cards
body:
## Symptoms
Card authorization response times exceed 2 seconds and the decline rate for reason code 91 (issuer unavailable) rises above 1 percent.

## Cause
Common causes are database connection pool exhaustion on the authorization hosts, a degraded load balancer pool, or a slow fraud scoring call.

## Resolution
1. Raise a P1 major incident immediately; card authorization is a critical service.
2. Check the Card Authorization service map for red CIs and open alerts from the last 15 minutes.
3. If the load balancer pool shows members down, fail traffic over to the secondary data centre using the documented change model.
4. If the fraud scoring call is slow, enable stand-in mode so low-value transactions are approved by the stand-in rules; this requires approval from the duty payments manager.
5. Post updates to the major incident bridge every 15 minutes until response times are below 1 second for 30 minutes.

title: ACH batch file rejected by pre-submission validation
author: kb.author.payments
body:
## Symptoms
The outbound ACH batch is held with status VALIDATION_FAILED and the cut-off time is approaching.

## Cause
The file contains a malformed record, most often an invalid routing number check digit or a batch control total that does not match the entries.

## Resolution
1. Open the validation report in the payments console and note the failing record numbers.
2. Do not edit the file by hand. Return the failing entries to the originating team through the exceptions queue.
3. Re-generate the batch without the failing entries and re-run validation.
4. If the cut-off will be missed, notify the duty payments manager so customers can be informed.
5. Record the record numbers and root cause in the incident for the monthly payments quality review.

title: Wire transfer gateway message queue backlog
author: kb.author.payments
body:
## Symptoms
Outgoing wire messages stay in status QUEUED for more than 10 minutes and the queue depth alert fires on the wire transfer gateway.

## Cause
The gateway consumer has stopped after a failed message, or the downstream network connection is down.

## Resolution
1. Check the queue depth dashboard and the consumer status on both gateway nodes.
2. If a single poison message is blocking the queue, move it to the exception queue using the operator console; never delete it.
3. Restart the consumer service on the affected node and confirm the queue depth starts to fall.
4. If the downstream connection is down, raise a P2 incident with CB-Network-Ops and inform the treasury desk of the expected delay.

title: Teller receipt printer not printing
author: kb.author.branch
body:
## Symptoms
The teller application completes the transaction but no receipt is printed, or the printer light blinks orange.

## Cause
Usually a paper jam, an empty paper roll, or the printer USB connection was lost after a workstation restart.

## Resolution
1. Open the printer cover, remove any jammed paper and check that a paper roll is loaded with the shiny side facing the print head.
2. Unplug and reconnect the USB cable, then restart the teller application.
3. Print a test receipt from the teller application settings page.
4. If the light still blinks orange, swap the printer with the branch spare and raise a hardware request for the faulty unit.

title: Unlock an Active Directory account
author: kb.author.identity
body:
## Symptoms
The user sees The referenced account is currently locked out and cannot sign in to the workstation or email.

## Cause
Too many failed sign-in attempts, often from an old password saved on a mobile device or a mapped drive.

## Resolution
1. Verify the caller's identity using the standard service desk verification questions.
2. Unlock the account in the directory management console; do not reset the password unless the user asks.
3. Ask the user to remove saved credentials from mobile mail apps and mapped drives to stop repeat lockouts.
4. If the account locks again within one hour, check the lockout source in the security log and escalate to CB-Identity-Ops.

title: Disk space alert on Linux application servers
author: kb.author.linux
body:
## Symptoms
Monitoring raises a Minor alert when /var or /opt is above 85 percent and a Major alert above 95 percent.

## Cause
Application logs that are not rotated, core dumps, or old deployment packages left on the server.

## Resolution
1. Run du -xh --max-depth=2 on the affected filesystem to find the largest directories.
2. Compress or remove application logs older than 14 days according to the log retention standard.
3. Remove deployment packages older than the last two releases from /opt/deploy/archive.
4. Never delete files from /var/lib or database directories; escalate to the owning team instead.
5. If usage returns above 85 percent within a week, raise a problem record so log rotation can be fixed.

title: Database connection pool exhausted on Payments Gateway
author: kb.author.payments
body:
## Symptoms
Payments Gateway logs show Timeout waiting for connection from pool and API response times climb above 3 seconds.

## Cause
Long-running queries or connections that are not returned to the pool after an error.

## Resolution
1. Check the database active sessions for the payments schema and identify sessions running longer than 60 seconds.
2. Capture the SQL text and execution plan of the long-running sessions before taking any action.
3. Restart one gateway node at a time to release leaked connections, keeping at least one node in service.
4. Do not increase the pool size during an incident without approval, because it can overload the database.
5. Raise a problem record with the captured SQL for the application team.

title: Renew an expiring TLS certificate
author: kb.author.security
body:
## Symptoms
The certificate expiry report shows a certificate expiring within 30 days, or users see a browser warning.

## Cause
Certificates are issued for a fixed validity period and must be renewed before they expire.

## Resolution
1. Raise a standard change using the certificate renewal template at least 10 business days before expiry.
2. Generate a new private key and certificate signing request on the server; never reuse the old key.
3. Submit the request through the internal certificate authority portal and attach the approval.
4. Install the new certificate and the full chain, then restart the service in the approved change window.
5. Verify the new expiry date with an external check and update the certificate inventory record.

title: MID Server shows Down or Validation failed
author: kb.author.platform
body:
## Symptoms
The MID Server record shows status Down, or Validated is false after an upgrade, and Discovery or integrations that use it stop.

## Cause
The MID Server service stopped on the host, the host lost outbound HTTPS access to the instance, or the MID Server needs to be re-validated after an upgrade.

## Resolution
1. Check that the MID Server service is running on the host and review the agent log for errors.
2. Confirm the host can reach the instance on port 443 through the proxy.
3. If the MID Server was upgraded, run the Validate related link on the MID Server record.
4. Check that the MID Server user account is not locked and still has the mid_server role.
5. After recovery, re-run any Discovery schedules that failed during the outage.

title: Discovery fails with credential errors on Windows servers
author: kb.author.platform
body:
## Symptoms
Discovery status shows Authentication failure or Access is denied for Windows servers, and the CIs are not updated.

## Cause
The Windows discovery credential has expired, has not been granted local administrator rights on new servers, or WMI is blocked by the host firewall.

## Resolution
1. Test the credential against the target from the MID Server using the credential test feature.
2. Confirm the discovery service account is in the server's local administrators group through group policy.
3. Check that WMI and remote procedure call ports are allowed from the MID Server subnet.
4. Re-run Discovery for the IP range and confirm the CI last discovered date updates.

title: Request access to a shared network drive
author: kb.author.servicedesk
body:
## Symptoms
The user needs read or write access to a departmental shared drive.

## Resolution
1. Submit the Shared Drive Access catalog item and choose the drive from the list.
2. The request is routed to the drive owner for approval.
3. After approval, access is granted automatically within one hour; the user must sign out and back in to see the drive.

title: Retrieve a BitLocker recovery key
author: kb.author.endpoint
body:
## Symptoms
The laptop asks for a BitLocker recovery key at start-up, often after a firmware update or docking station change.

## Cause
BitLocker detected a change in the boot configuration and requires the recovery key to unlock the disk.

## Resolution
1. Verify the caller's identity with the standard verification questions and confirm the laptop asset tag.
2. Look up the recovery key by the key ID shown on the laptop screen in the endpoint management console.
3. Read the key to the user; never send it by email or chat.
4. After the laptop starts, ask the user to restart once more to confirm it no longer asks for the key.
5. Record in the ticket that the key was disclosed so it is rotated automatically.

title: Mobile banking login errors spike - triage
author: kb.author.digital
body:
## Symptoms
The mobile banking login failure rate rises above 5 percent, or customers report Something went wrong at login.

## Cause
Typical causes are an expired certificate on the API gateway, an identity provider outage, or a mobile app release with a configuration error.

## Resolution
1. Check the Mobile API service map and the identity provider status page for active alerts.
2. Compare the failure rate by app version; if only the newest version fails, ask the release manager to pause the staged rollout.
3. Check the API gateway certificate expiry date.
4. If the failure rate stays above 5 percent for 10 minutes, raise a P1 major incident and inform the customer contact centre so they can update the phone message.

title: End-of-day batch overrun - escalation procedure
author: kb.author.batch
body:
## Symptoms
The end-of-day batch has not reached the interest accrual step by 01:30 and the online day for branches is at risk.

## Cause
Upstream files arrived late, a job failed and was restarted, or database contention slowed the batch.

## Resolution
1. Check the batch scheduler for failed or long-running jobs and the arrival times of upstream files.
2. If a job failed, restart it only from the documented restart point for that job.
3. At 02:00 inform the duty operations manager with the expected completion time.
4. If the online day cannot start on time, follow the delayed start procedure in KB0010024.

title: Statement generation job failure
author: kb.author.batch
body:
## Symptoms
The monthly statement generation job ends with a non-zero return code and fewer statement files than expected are produced.

## Cause
A customer record with invalid address data, or the output storage share running out of space.

## Resolution
1. Read the job log and identify the last customer record processed.
2. If the failure is a data error, move the record to the exceptions list and restart the job from the checkpoint.
3. If the storage share is full, ask CB-Storage-Ops to extend it before restarting.
4. Reconcile the number of generated statements with the expected count before release to the print vendor.

title: Fraud alert queue backlog
author: kb.author.fraud
body:
## Symptoms
The fraud case queue holds more than 200 unworked high-risk alerts or the oldest alert is older than 30 minutes.

## Cause
A rule change that generates too many alerts, a surge in genuine fraud attempts, or analysts unable to reach the case tool.

## Resolution
1. Check whether a scoring rule was changed in the last 24 hours and compare alert volume by rule.
2. If one rule is responsible, ask the fraud strategy lead to approve a temporary threshold change.
3. Prioritise card-not-present alerts above 500 in local currency.
4. If analysts cannot reach the case tool, raise a P2 incident against the Fraud Analytics service.

title: Add a network printer in a branch
author: kb.author.branch
body:
## Resolution
Open Printers, choose Add, pick the branch printer from the list.

title: Fix audio problems in online meetings
author: kb.author.endpoint
body:
## Symptoms
Other participants cannot hear the user, or the user hears echo or robotic audio during online meetings.

## Cause
The wrong audio device is selected, the headset firmware is outdated, or the network connection is congested.

## Resolution
1. In the meeting app device settings, select the headset for both microphone and speaker and run the test call.
2. Unplug other audio devices such as webcams with built-in microphones.
3. Update the headset firmware from the software centre.
4. If audio is robotic, ask the user to move closer to the wireless access point or use a wired connection.

title: Change freeze and emergency change procedure
author: kb.author.change
body:
## Summary
During change freeze periods, such as quarter end and peak trading days, only emergency changes are permitted.

## Resolution
1. Confirm whether the change is needed to restore service or to prevent an imminent outage; otherwise it must wait until the freeze ends.
2. Raise an emergency change linked to the incident or problem record.
3. Obtain approval from the emergency change advisory board through the on-call change manager.
4. Implement with a documented back-out plan and a second engineer reviewing each step.
5. Complete a post-implementation review within two business days.

title: Reset a password for the core banking teller application
author: kb.author.identity
body:
## Symptoms
The teller cannot sign in to the core banking teller application because the password has expired or been forgotten.

## Cause
Teller application passwords expire every 60 days and are separate from the workstation sign-in.

## Resolution
1. Direct the user to the self-service password page from a branch workstation; it requires MFA approval.
2. If self-service is not possible, verify identity with the branch manager call-back procedure before resetting.
3. Set a temporary password that must be changed at first sign-in and give it to the user by phone only.
4. Never ask the user to tell you their current or new password.

title: Delayed start of the online banking day (legacy procedure)
author: kb.author.batch
body:
## Resolution
1. Call the legacy operations hotline.
2. Switch branches to offline mode using the old teller console.
This procedure was replaced when the teller platform was upgraded.

title: Message streaming consumer lag on the events platform
author: kb.author.integration
body:
## Symptoms
Consumer lag on the account events topic grows continuously and downstream systems receive events late.

## Cause
A consumer instance is stuck, or the consumer group is rebalancing repeatedly.

## Resolution
1. Check the consumer group status and the number of active members.
2. Restart stuck consumer instances one at a time.
3. If rebalancing repeats, review the session timeout setting with the integration team.
